correctness.rationale: The private-line bijection proves the enumerator formula for all 2^13 point subsets. The explicit complete tangent profile census is reproduced by a standalone verifier, and an independent C++ conflict-graph recursion constructs the full 52-edge object and checks all 10,700 matchings, size polynomial, exactly 1,404 unique five-flag extensions, 1,989+234 maximal sets and absence of size five maximal sets. Generated projective group order 5,616 plus duality, with checked orbit certificate, establishes 12 disjoint orbits. The proof and computations apply to PG(2,3) only.

originality.rationale: 1991 Illés–Szőnyi–Wettl supplies the equivalent SRS definition, general maximality bounds and smallest-size structural criterion; 2008 Kiss–Marcugini–Pambianco classifies q=3 semioval size and class. These are duly credited. The combined full 10,700-system induced-matching polynomial and all-size saturation census, especially unique size-five completion, is not stated nor implied by those inspected results. Targeted published-finding, title, parameter, coefficient and equivalence searches found no complete prior result, subject to unindexed historical classification risk. The Mengyán (2008) paper on non-prime-order flag partitions was compared by publisher abstract but full PDF access was not obtained, which remains a specifically recorded priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The classical finite-plane SRS problem motivates a complete finite incidence invariant rather than a contrived small slice. Resolving the entire induced-matching polynomial, complete saturation sizes, all 12 orbit types, and the rigid unique optimal extension of every five-flag system provides geometric/combinatorial information not implied by existing maximal-size bounds or small semioval classification. In particular, the absent maximal size-five layer despite 1,404 five-systems is a natural structural boundary and useful benchmark for flag conflict graphs.
